sources.title: Unicode 17.0 NamesList
sources.location: NamesList search for the initial filter-response terminology
sources.direct_observation: The NamesList does not contain semantic character names for high-pass filter, low-pass filter, band-pass filter, band-stop filter, low cut, high cut, equalizer, or filter.
sources.interpretation: No existing Unicode semantic equivalent was identified for the initial research set. This does not by itself establish a need for new characters.
sources.rights_note: Reference only; no Unicode glyph artwork is imported.

sources.title: Ableton Live 8.1 Manual
sources.direct_observation: The EQ Eight interface documentation depicts selectable response forms labeled Low Cut, Low Shelf, Bell, Notch, High Shelf, and High Cut.
sources.interpretation: This is product-UI evidence for a compact response-form family. It does not prove portable plain-text character use or authorize reuse of Ableton artwork.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Filters and EQ Tutorial
sources.direct_observation: The tutorial describes and illustrates low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, and band-stop filtering as frequency-response concepts.
sources.interpretation: The terminology and response semantics are educationally stable. This is not direct evidence for a standalone text character.
sources.rights_note: Linked as evidence.

sources.title: IEC 60617 graphical symbols database
sources.location: Public database landing page; individual record verification remains required
sources.direct_observation: The cited portal is the IEC 60617 graphical-symbols database reference.
sources.interpretation: IEC circuit-diagram filter symbols and terminology are adjacent semantic evidence, not direct evidence for the compact audio-community response glyph target. Individual records require page-level citation before stronger claims are made.
sources.rights_note: Do not copy IEC artwork without permission.

sources.title: DSSSP icon font mapping
sources.direct_observation: The stylesheet maps a filter-response icon family to custom-font code points.
sources.interpretation: Custom font mappings can supply visual response symbols in software but are not portable plain-text interchange.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only.

sources.title: Live 12 Manual: Live Audio Effect Reference
sources.location: EQ Eight and filter/equalizer effect reference
sources.direct_observation: The current manual documents named filter and EQ response modes within a product interface.
sources.interpretation: This supports continued product use of the response semantics, but not portable plain-text character use or a single required glyph contour.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Pro-Q: Band Controls
sources.location: Band controls and EQ display documentation
sources.direct_observation: The documentation describes selectable EQ filter shapes and an interactive frequency-response display.
sources.interpretation: This is evidence of a mature response-form UI family; its rich, contextual display is not evidence of an established standalone text glyph.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Kontakt Manual: Filter Reference
sources.direct_observation: The manual names filter types and parameters in product documentation.
sources.interpretation: Named and abbreviated terminology can carry the semantics without a compact standalone response symbol.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: MONTAGE M Owner's Manual: Filter Parameters
sources.direct_observation: The current documentation presents filter-type terminology in parameter and screen context.
sources.interpretation: This corroborates the semantic vocabulary while also showing that textual labels and contextual UI can be preferred over an independent glyph.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Logic Pro for iPad User Guide: Filters
sources.direct_observation: The user guide documents filter effects and their controls in a mainstream DAW.
sources.interpretation: This is cross-vendor evidence for the category, not proof that a particular response sketch functions as portable plain text.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Cubase Pro 15 Plug-in Reference: Effect Modules
sources.direct_observation: The reference presents filter functions with textual control and parameter terminology.
sources.interpretation: The semantic class appears in current DAW documentation, but the representation is not a portable text-character practice.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Moog Matriarch Filter Modes
sources.direct_observation: The manufacturer documents selectable synthesizer filter modes by name.
sources.interpretation: This adds synthesizer-hardware evidence for stable semantics while leaving symbol-form and text-interchange questions open.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Getting Started: Filters
sources.direct_observation: The manufacturer explains filter categories and response behavior for synthesizer users.
sources.interpretation: This independently corroborates the response vocabulary, not a standard compact glyph or plain-text encoding need.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: ARP 2600 Owner's Manual
sources.direct_observation: The manual documents a low-pass voltage-controlled filter and presents frequency-response material in labeled, axis-bearing explanatory form.
sources.interpretation: This is early evidence for the filter-response semantics, not evidence of an axis-less compact response glyph.
sources.rights_note: Linked historical source only; no artwork is reproduced or traced.

sources.title: Legacy Synthesizer Manual Download
sources.direct_observation: Korg hosts an official legacy-synthesizer manual download relevant to the historical-source corpus.
sources.interpretation: This is a reproducible primary-source acquisition point, retained without making a glyph-lineage claim until page-level review is recorded.
sources.rights_note: Do not reproduce or trace manual artwork without permission.

sources.title: JUPITER-8 Retrospective
sources.direct_observation: Roland's retrospective describes the 1981 JUPITER-8 as having a low-pass VCF and a non-resonant high-pass filter.
sources.interpretation: This corroborates historical use of the semantic pair, but a retrospective is not evidence of a period-specific compact symbol drawing.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: FabFilter Software Instruments Announce Pro-Q
sources.direct_observation: The launch announcement names Bell, shelf, and cut filter forms for Pro-Q.
sources.interpretation: This supports a documented 2009 software-EQ vocabulary, not a conclusion that one compact response drawing had already converged across products.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: Synthesizer Parameter Manual
sources.location: LPF, HPF, BPF, and BEF response illustrations
sources.direct_observation: The manual illustrates LPF, HPF, BPF, and band-eliminate filtering with axis-bearing response diagrams.
sources.interpretation: This is direct evidence for the four response semantics, while its explanatory graphs are counterevidence to treating the diagrams as established axis-less standalone glyphs.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; product artwork is not copied or traced.

sources.title: High-Pass and Low-Pass Filters
sources.direct_observation: The article refers to filter controls as bent-line icons on microphones, mixing boards, and plug-ins while explaining high-pass and low-pass behavior.
sources.interpretation: This supports a recognizable visual UI convention, but the article itself communicates the meanings with prose and images rather than a portable text glyph.
sources.rights_note: Linked as evidence; no article images are reproduced.

sources.title: Types of EQ
sources.direct_observation: The instructional article explains common EQ and filter types with semantic names and visual response explanations.
sources.interpretation: This is terminology and educational-visual evidence, not evidence that practitioners use an encoded response character in ordinary text.
sources.rights_note: Linked as evidence; no article images are reproduced.

sources.title: I need help figuring out what this symbol means
sources.location: Question and replies about an audio control symbol
sources.direct_observation: A user asks the community to identify an audio-related symbol shown in an image.
sources.interpretation: This is evidence of recognition friction around visual controls, not evidence of a standard text-form response glyph.
sources.rights_note: Linked discussion only; user content is not reproduced.

sources.title: EQ symbols
sources.direct_observation: A forum participant seeks to describe or identify EQ symbols in a text discussion.
sources.interpretation: The thread suggests a text-description workaround for a visual control, but does not establish a shared compact character in portable plain text.
sources.rights_note: Linked discussion only; user content is not reproduced.

sources.title: I keep mixing up low pass and high pass
sources.location: Question and replies about filter terminology
sources.direct_observation: A user reports confusion between low-pass and high-pass terminology in a production discussion.
sources.interpretation: This is evidence that the semantic labels can be confused, not evidence that an icon or encoded glyph resolves the confusion.
sources.rights_note: Linked discussion only; user content is not reproduced.

sources.title: Filter terminology discussion
sources.direct_observation: Participants discuss filter terminology and distinctions in an audio-software community forum.
sources.interpretation: Terminology variation is a material counterexample to assuming a single unambiguous label or symbol without corpus-backed semantic boundaries.
sources.rights_note: Linked discussion only; user content is not reproduced.

sources.title: FontAudio
sources.direct_observation: The project supplies audio-oriented UI icons through a dedicated icon-font project.
sources.interpretation: A dedicated font can fill a UI-icon gap, but its glyph mappings are not proof of interoperable Unicode characters or ordinary plain-text use.
sources.rights_note: Evidence only; do not import icon artwork or font data without separate license review.
